 JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 22 of The Employee's Compensation Act, 1923, seeking compensation of Rs.25,50,000/- from the respondents on account of death of Maruthi S., who is son of petitioner No.1 and 2 and brother of petitioner No.3, during the course of employment.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
The deceased Maruthi S., in the course of his employment under the respondent No.1 and while discharging his duty as a driver of bus bearing Reg. No. KA- 01-AC-4960,
as per the instructions of the respondent No.1/owner of the said vehicle, encountered with an accident, sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to said injuries.
The deceased was a driver in the said vehicle, which traveled from Mysore to Horanadu.

On 15-02-2020 at about 7.30 p.m., after returning from Sringeri Temple, on Karkala-Sringeri Highway, near National Highway, Abbas Kattingeri, Mala Village,
Udupi, Karnataka, the deceased drove the bus in a high speed, rash and negligent manner, without observing traffic rules and regulations and turned the vehicle.

Due to which, the said bus dashed against the right side of the heavy rock, consequently the bus got crushed, resulting in death of 6 male passengers, 3 female passengers on the spot, including the driver of the bus and other passengers have sustained severe injuries.
The deceased driver was shifted to Karkala Government Hospital.
The doctors examined him and declared to be dead on the spot.

Earlier to the accident,

sentences.text: the deceased was working as a driver under the respondent No.1 and drawing salary of Rs.20,000/- per month and he was getting bata of Rs.200/- per day.
He was contributing his entire earnings to his family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.
The Karkala Rural Police have registered the case against the deceased driver of the said bus for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337, 338 and 304(A) of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.25,50,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent.

Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.
4.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of bus bearing No. KA-01-AC-4960 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

It is further contended that, as on the date of accident the deceased was not working under the respondent No.1,
as such there was no relationship of master and servant between the respondent No.1 and the deceased.
It has further contended that, the deceased was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the offending bus at the time of accident.
At the time of accident The deceased was not having licence to drive transport vehicle and he was eligible to driver only Light Motor Vehicle (LMV).
Whereas the vehicle involved in the accident was Heavy Transport Vehicle (HTV).
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the deceased.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioners prove that, there was employee and employer relationship between the deceased Maruthi S., and the respondent No.1 ?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that, during the course of employment the deceased Maruthi S., has died, due to the injuries sustained in the accident that occurred on 15-02-2020 ?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
4.

What order or Award ?

Issue No.1: Negative.

REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioners that, the deceased Maruthi S., was an employee of respondent No.1 and he was working as a driver in the bus bearing Reg. No. KA-01-AC-4960,
belonging to the respondent No.1.

On 15-02-2020 at about 7.30 p.m., after returning from Sringeri Temple, on Karkala-Sringeri Highway, near National Highway, Abbas Kattingeri, Mala Village,
Udupi, Karnataka, the deceased drove the bus in a high speed, rash and negligent manner, without observing traffic rules and regulations and turned the vehicle.

Due to which, the said bus dashed against the right side of the heavy rock, consequently the bus got crushed, resulting in death of 6 male passengers, 3 female passengers on the spot, including the driver of the bus.
Earlier to the accident, the deceased was working as a driver under the respondent No.1 and drawing salary of Rs.20,000/- per month and he was getting bata of Rs.200/- per day.
He was contributing his entire earnings to his family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.

10. At the outset it is pertinent to note that, in the instant case, there is no dispute that, as on the date of alleged accident, the respondent No.1 was the owner of bus bearing Reg. No. KA-01-AC-4960 and the respondent No.2 was the insurer of said vehicle.
Further, the alleged date, time and place of accident, the involvement of bus bearing Reg. No. KA-01-AC-4960 in the accident is also not in dispute.

In order to claim compensation from the respondents under Sec.22 of the Employee's Compensation Act, 1923, the foremost burden on the petitioners is to establish that, as on the alleged date, time and place of accident, the deceased Maruti was an employee of the respondent No.1 and as per the instructions of the respondent No.1, he was working as a driver in the offending bus No. KA-01-AC-4960, owned by the respondent No.1.
The petitioners have to prove that, at the time of accident there was an employer and employee relationship between the respondent No.1 and the deceased Maruti.

sentences.text: In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 has got examined herself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein she has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of their oral evidence, the petitioners have got marked total 13 documents as Ex.P.1 to 13.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of spot mahazar,
Ex.P.3 is true copy of sketch, Ex.P.4 is true copy of notice U/Sec.133 M.V. Act, Ex.P.5 is true copy of reply to said notice, Ex.P.6 is true copy of seizure mahazar, Ex.P.7 is true copy of Mototr Vehicle Accident report, Ex.P.8 is true copy of post-mortem report, Ex.P.9 is true copy of charge-sheet,

Ex.P10 is notarised copy of Aadhar card of petitioner No.2, Ex.P,11 is notarised copy of Aadhar card of petitioner No.1, Ex.P.12 is true copy of first information statement and Ex.P13 is driving licence extract.

12. The petitioner No.1/P.W.1 has deposed in her evidence that, at the time of accident, the deceased Maruthi S., was an employee of respondent No.1 and he was working as a driver in the bus bearing Reg. No. KA-01-AC-4960, belonging to the respondent No.1.

Further she has deposed that, on 15-02-2020 at about 7.30 p.m., after returning from Sringeri Temple, on Karkala-Sringeri Highway,
near National Highway, Abbas Kattingeri, Mala Village, Udupi, Karnataka, the deceased drove the bus in a high speed, rash and negligent manner, without observing traffic rules and regulations and turned the vehicle.

Due to which, the said bus dashed against the right side of the heavy rock,
consequently the bus got crushed, resulting in death of 6 male passengers, 3 female passengers on the spot, including the deceased driver Maruti.

The above oral & documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners has remained undisputed by the respondent No.1/owner of offending vehicle, as he did not choose to appear and contest the case of the petitioners.

Whereas, the respondent No.2 has specifically denied the alleged fact that, at the time of accident, the deceased Maruthi S., was an employee of respondent No.1 and he was working as a driver in the bus bearing Reg. No. KA-01-AC-4960, belonging to the respondent No.1.

In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioners to prove that, at the time of accident, the deceased Maruthi S., was an employee of respondent No.1 and he was working as a driver in the bus bearing Reg. No. KA-01-AC-4960,
belonging to the respondent No.1.
13.

But, it is pertinent to note that, except the self serving statements of the petitioners and the oral evidence of P.W.1, there is absolutely no other oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners to show that, at the time of accident, the deceased Maruthi S., was an employee of respondent No.1 and he was working as a driver in the bus bearing Reg. No. KA-01-AC-4960,
belonging to the respondent No.1.

The petitioners have not produced any document to show that, at the time of accident the deceased Maruti was holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the offending bus bearing Reg. No. KA-01-AC-4960.

Further, the petitioners have not produced any document to show that, at the time of accident, the deceased Maruti was the employee of respondent No.1 and as per the instructions of respondent No.1 he was working as a driver in the bus bearing Reg. No. KA-01-AC-4960.
Even, there is absolutely no evidence on record to show that, at any point of time the deceased Maruti had worked under the respondent No.1 or he was the employee of respondent No.1.

If no documents were available with the petitioners to establish the same, the petitioners ought to have made an effort to examine atleast the respondent No.1 to prove that, the Drakshayanamma vs Basavaraju on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124457658/

sentences.text: deceased Maruti was his employee at the time of accident or any other employee of respondent No.1.

But, the petitioner have not made any efforts to examine the respondent No.1 or any other witness,
for the reasons best known to them.

In such circumstances, it leads this Court to draw adverse inference against the petitioners and hold that, at the time of accident the deceased Maruti was not an employee of the respondent No.1 and there was no employer and employee relationship between them.

14. On the other hand, as per the document produced by the petitioners themselves i.e. Ex.P.5 reply to notice issued U/Sec.133 of Motor Vehicles Act, given by the respondent No.1, one Vijay was the permanent driver of offending bus bearing No. KA-01-AC-4960.

As the said Vijay was on leave on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 had deputed one Radha Ravi R., to drive the said bus and handed over the said bus to him on 14-02-2020 at 9:30 p.m. Thereafter, when the respondent No.1 came to Karkal Rural Police Station, he came to know that, the said Radha Ravi had taken his friend deceased Maruti along with him in the said bus and at the time of accident the said Maruti was driving the bus.
Further, as per Ex.P.9 charge-sheet filed by the investigation officer, the said accident has occurred due to sole rash and negligent driving of deceased Maruti.

Further, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.1 has not denied the suggestion made by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 that, as per Ex.P.5 the respondent No.1 has stated that, at the time of accident, the deceased Maruti was not his employee and as on the date of accident one Radha Ravi was the driver of bus bearing No. KA-01-AC-4960.
But, she has pleaded her ignorance about the said fact, stating that she doesn't know about it.

In such circumstances and for the above stated reasons, there is no other option before this Court, except to hold that, the petitioners have failed to prove through cogent and corroborative evidence that, as on the date of accident the deceased Maruti was the employee of respondent No.1 and as per the instructions of respondent No.1, the deceased Maruti was driving the offending bus at the time of accident.
As such, the petitioners have failed to prove that, at the time of accident there was employee and employer relationship between the deceased Maruthi S., and the respondent No.1.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Negative.
15. Issue No.2 & 3:

As per Sec.3(1) of the Employee's Compensation Act, 1923, the employer is liable to pay the compensation only in case if any personal injury is caused to his employee by an accident arising out of and in the course of his employment.

In the instant case, as the petitioners have failed to prove the very existence of employee and employer relationship between the respondent No.1 and deceased Maruthi and also failed to prove that, the deceased Maruti has died due to injuries caused during the course of his employment, the question of paying compensation to the petitioners, who are the legal representatives of deceased Maruti, by the respondent No.1, does not arise at all.
In such circumstances, the Issue No.2 & 3 does not survive for consideration.

Hence, I answer Issue No.2 & 3 in Negative.
16.
Issue No.4:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is dismissed with costs.
Draw award accordingly.
